newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares edge up at close, Lion Nathan eases.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares edge up at close, Lion Nathan eases.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices edge up at close
* Lion Nathan upward run reversed
* Bid for Underground Fashions progresses swiftly
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
340 +2 * NZSC cap index +2.45 at 5,115.18
374 -5 * Volume NZ$49.4 million. Futures +5 at 1,212
744 +1 * Other movers - +25 +5
New Zealand share prices closed modestly firmer on Thursday but the steam went out of Lion Nathan's rumour-driven share price.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 7.90 points higher at 2,400.50 on turnover worth NZ$49.4 million.

Lion, the subject of takeover rumour since the start of the year, eased back five to NZ$3.74 after a strong, speculative run. Lion again acted to quell the talk, saying it was "just rumours", but it persisted, nevertheless.

Don Turkington at Cavill White Securities said it was disppointing the market had not followed through on Wall Street's 84-point gain, but suggested bearish sentiment in the money markets may be the reason.
Lion had taken a breather, but again on big turnover of 2.9 million shares, worth NZ$10.94 million.
While it was anyone's guess as to whether the rumour had any veracity, Turkington said it appeared the activity was based on speculation the stock may eventually come into play.
"Certainly a number of investors are speculating that, where there is smoke, there is fire," Turkington said.
A handful of mid-sized stocks attracted higher than normal interest.
Among them were Fisher and Paykel, a line of 200,000 going through at NZ$5.28; Sanford, with 150,000 trading at $3.10; and Wrightson, 100,000 going through at $1.05.
Forest group Carter Holt Harvey was performing strongly, gaining two to NZ$3.40.
The bid by Australia's Just Jeans for Underground progressed swiftly after receiving the independent director's approval.
